title: ai_content_review_checklist
claim: AI content review requires testing specific factual claims against verified operational sources, not just editing prose.
hook: Fluent writing is not evidence of a true claim.

evidence.detail: An editorial checklist protocol establishing a three-part source test (existence, fit, currency) and operational verification gates for AI-generated brand claims.

slides.headline: Fluent writing is not evidence of a true claim.
Extract assertions before reviewing grammar.
slides.body: Isolate every statistic, date, and comparison into a clean ledger. Verify facts independently of sentence flow.

items.label: Assign ownership
items.detail: Match each claim to a verified source

slides.headline: Apply the three-part source test.
slides.body: Confirm existence, fit, and currency. A source must be real, relevant to your market, and currently valid.

items.label: Currency check
items.detail: Ensure terms and regulations are active

slides.headline: Verify product promises with operations.
slides.body: Language from old sales collateral can state uncontracted terms. Route capability claims directly to owners.

slides.headline: Set approval gates by exposure level.
slides.body: General copy needs standard editing. Claims touching safety, compliance, or financial data require expert sign-off.

slides.headline: Run this review sequence on every draft.
slides.body: Enforce basic verification gates before publishing any AI-generated industrial collateral.

items.label: Data audit
items.detail: No confidential inputs leaked to public tools

slides.headline: Steal these review rules for your team.
slides.body: Can the named author defend every fact in this draft? If not, the piece is not ready to publish.

items.label: The Author Test
items.detail: Author can explain and defend all facts

items.label: Source Traceability
items.detail: Every claim traces to a primary document

slides.headline: Proof lives in operations, not language.
slides.body: A draft is ready to go live only when the professional named on it can personally defend every underlying assertion.

caption:
Fluent writing is not evidence of a true claim.

When evaluating AI content within a B2B brand strategy, polished prose often masks unsupported assumptions. Generative models produce authoritative language by default, regardless of whether the underlying facts match your operating reality.

Fixing style is easy; verifying accuracy is where reputational risk lives. If a draft claims a service capability or regulatory standard that operations cannot deliver, smooth sentence structure only accelerates commercial exposure.

Reviewing the claims ledger instead of paragraph syntax isolates the risk early. If the named author cannot defend the primary source behind a specific metric, the piece stays in draft.

The complete editorial framework is published on my site: https://www.rachitmishra.in/2026/10/27/ai-content-review-checklist/

Send this to the communications lead managing your editorial sign-off queue.
